_schema.description: Curated geopolitical event registry per docs/019_Geopolitical_Intelligence.md. Every event must carry sources (invariant: no unverified data). severity and oil_supply_impact are 0-10; confidence is 0-1. status: active | monitoring | resolved. Resolved events are kept forever (invariant: historical information must remain preserved).

events.description: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-02-28 following the US/Israel air campaign. Partially reopened in early July 2026 after a US-Iran MoU, then re-closed on 2026-07-13 amid renewed exchanges. Ships attacked in the strait 2026-07-07; US strikes on Iran followed 2026-07-11. IRGC declares the strait closed; CENTCOM reports reduced traffic via the southern Omani corridor only. ~25% of seaborne oil trade transits this chokepoint.

Active military conflict between the US/Israel and Iran since late February 2026, including ongoing missile exchanges as of mid-July 2026. Drives the Hormuz closure and poses direct risk to Gulf production, export terminals, and shipping.

De-escalation diplomacy has shifted to Muscat: an Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi visited Oman for talks on reopening the strait; France and Britain are studying Omani-drafted proposals for IMO-supervised navigational fees. Mediation channels are strained (Oman and Qatar both struck by Iran on 2026-07-12; Pakistan track suspended). Headlines around these talks whipsaw prices in both directions.
